title: The ethics, looking back
tomorrow: a restless heart. where does Augustine say it finally rests?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ways of prayer: hours, a breath, a scene, a silence, a shout. Your way to pray. Today, how all of it gets lived.
screen: `YOUR WAY TO PRAY.` → `HOW IT GETS LIVED.`

segments.voice: Comment sections run on rules: who broke which one, who should be called out. In a letter to Rome, Paul runs through the old commandments: don't commit adultery, don't kill, don't steal, don't covet. Then he folds the whole page in half. Every one, he says, is summed up in one saying: love your neighbor as yourself. So, one question for today: what sits at the center of a good life?
screen: `WHO BROKE WHICH RULE.` → `THE PAGE, FOLDED IN HALF.` → `WHAT SITS AT THE CENTER?`

segments.voice: Paul's answer: “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.” Love doesn't cancel the commandments; it fills them. Not stealing is what love looks like around someone's wallet. The virtues get the same treatment: Colossians lists kindness, humility, meekness and patience like clothes, then says, “And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.” Charity is the King James word for love. And mercy is love when someone has failed. Jesus says: “Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.” Now a neighbor who puts mercy near the center too. In Islam, a hadith, a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, recorded by al-Tirmidhi, runs like this in paraphrase: the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; be merciful to those on earth, and the One in heaven will be merciful to you. Shared ground: mercy given and mercy received belong together. And one honest difference. For Christians, mercy has a face in Jesus, whom they call God's Son, and in his cross. Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as God's Son, and the Qur'an calls the Prophet Muhammad a mercy to the worlds. Two neighbors, each listening to their own teacher, both saying: be merciful.
screen: `LOVE IS THE FULFILLING OF THE LAW.` · `ABOVE ALL, PUT ON CHARITY.` · `A NEIGHBOR: THE MERCIFUL SHOWN MERCY.` · `TWO TEACHERS, ONE WORD: MERCY.` · then, large: `LOVE FULFILS IT.`

segments.voice: Choose one person likely to need mercy from you this week, someone who'll be late, wrong or sharp. Name what makes mercy hard with them, and one small plan for the moment it comes: a pause, a softer word, a second chance. If you pray, hold their name with the beatitude: blessed are the merciful.
The ethics. Commandments, virtues and mercy, seen from three sides, with love at the center of all three.
For the road: love fulfils it, every commandment folded into one. Day twenty-six of the summit.

howItsDone: Christians learn the commandments in catechism classes and Sunday school, and some churches turn to Romans 13 or the Beatitudes when they talk about everyday choices; Muslims recall the Prophet's sayings on mercy and call on God as the Most Merciful.

Unity thread: shared = mercy shown and mercy received belong together. Christian side: Matthew 5:7 (KJV). Neighbor's own words, paraphrased (no quotation marks): the hadith 'the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; be merciful to those on earth, and the One in heaven will be merciful to you' (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1924; also in Sunan Abi Dawud 4941). Honest difference = Christians see mercy's face in Jesus as God's Son and his cross; Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not God's Son (Qur'an 4:171, 19:30), and the Qur'an calls the Prophet Muhammad a mercy to the worlds (21:107, paraphrased). No ranking. A Muslim reader should confirm the paraphrases, the hadith number and the fairness of the difference.
